Our mission

To create ocean experiences that inspire growth, connection and progress

Through personalized surf coaching, guided adventures, and a deep respect for nature, we help people move beyond simply learning to surf. Our purpose is to create space for confidence, discovery, and meaningful experiences in and out of the water.

Every session, tour, and coaching program is designed to help our guests connect with the ocean, explore the beauty of Costa Rica, and leave with a deeper understanding of both surfing and themselves.

My story

From a borrowed boogie board to Passing it On

My name is Mateo. I moved from Colombia to Costa Rica when I was 13 years old. At the time, I had never surfed, didn't even know how to swim, and knew absolutely nothing about the ocean or surfboards. One day, while walking along Tamarindo Beach, I saw people surfing and was instantly captivated. I told my mom I wanted to learn.

Before getting my first surfboard, a family friend gave me a boogie board. That's where it all started. I learned how to catch waves, understand the ocean, and even stand up on it.

One day, a surf instructor noticed me in the water and invited me onto one of his longboards. He pushed me into wave after wave, giving me guidance and encouragement along the way. That experience stayed with me and sparked something much bigger than a love for surfing.

Soon after, my mom bought me my first surfboard, and I was fortunate to meet a family who shared a deep passion for surfing. They became my mentors, teaching me about the ocean, helping me grow as a surfer, and passing on a connection and love for the sport that would shape my life.

Surfing taught me to respect the ocean, appreciate its beauty, and understand its constantly changing nature. More importantly, it showed me the power of sharing a passion with others. The same way that a surf instructor, a group of friends, and an entire community helped shape my journey, I now strive to pass that passion on to every person I have the privilege to teach.

Lean Forward was born from that purpose. My goal is not simply to teach people how to surf. It is to help them build confidence, connect with the ocean, discover what they are capable of, and experience the incredible feeling that comes from riding a wave.

Because sometimes, one wave can change much more than your day. It can change your life.

Lean Forward — Smooth Connection.

The Philosophy

At Lean Forward, surfing is more than learning a skill.

It's a way to connect with nature, build confidence, and develop a deeper understanding of yourself through the ocean.

Founded by Mateo in Tamarindo, Lean Forward combines professional surf coaching with authentic Costa Rican experiences designed to help you progress, explore, and reconnect.

Whether you're catching your very first wave or looking to refine years of experience, every session is built around your goals.

Who it's for

The Foundation is the starting point at Lean Forward. It works for two kinds of surfer: someone who has never stood on a board and wants a safe, patient introduction to the ocean, and someone who already catches waves but wants the technique broken down properly instead of guessing.

Because the format runs from a one-on-one private session up to a group of three or more, the coaching stays personal at every price point. What changes between the formats is how much of the session is direct attention, not how much care goes into it.

Where it leads

Once you are catching waves consistently in Tamarindo, The Exploration takes you to spots further along the Guanacaste coast, and The Immersion pairs a day of surfing with a half day of exploration.

Not sure you're ready to move on? Read 5 signs you're ready to move beyond beginner surf lessons.

For a full itinerary experience, the Signature Progression Week is the one to look at — a structured roadmap rather than isolated lessons, with video analysis, wave reading sessions and a written plan you keep after the trip.

The Exploration

Guided surf tours beyond Tamarindo

For intermediate surfers ready to discover the best waves on the Guanacaste coast.

Spots we explore

  • Playa Avellanas
  • Playa Grande
  • Guiones
  • Marbella

The destination is chosen on the day, based on swell, wind and tide.

What's included

  • 3-hour guided surf experience
  • Transportation guidance
  • Surf spot selection based on conditions
  • Board included
  • Snacks & hydration

Photo, video and drone packages are available at an extra, optional price.

Starting from $130 per person

Plan a tour

Why the spot changes

Guanacaste has a lot of coastline and no two beaches work on the same conditions. Rather than committing to a destination in advance, the spot is picked on the day so the group surfs where the swell, wind and tide actually line up.

That is the difference between a surf tour and a surf transfer: the point is not the drive, it is arriving somewhere that is working.

For a closer look at each break, read our local's guide to the best surf spots around Tamarindo.

Before you book

The Exploration assumes you can already catch and ride green waves independently and feel comfortable managing yourself in the water.

You don't need to be an expert. Mateo stays in the water with you throughout the session, offering in-water coaching, guidance and safety support to help you progress. The goal is to explore different breaks around the coast, like Playa Grande or Avellanas, while choosing conditions that match your level and comfort.

If you're still building your foundation, start with The Foundation in Tamarindo. The two can also work beautifully together during the same trip.

Surf Tips

5 signs you're ready to move beyond beginner surf lessons

How to know when it's time to trade the whitewater for open-face waves.

Surf Tips3 min read

Every surfer remembers the first time whitewater stopped feeling like a fight and started feeling like a ride. That shift doesn't happen on a fixed schedule — it happens whenever your body and your instincts catch up with each other. Here are five signs it's happening for you.

The 5 signs

  • You catch waves on your own

    In a first lesson, most of the work is done by the push: the coach reads the wave, times it, and gives you a shove into the whitewater. The first real sign of progress is when you stop needing that push — you're paddling into waves on your own timing, and catching more of them than you miss.

  • You're thinking about where you are, not just what you're doing

    Beginners are focused entirely on standing up. Somewhere in the process, the focus quietly shifts to positioning — where the peak is, where the whitewater will break, where the other people in the water are. If you've caught yourself paddling sideways before a set even arrives, that's a new instinct, not a coincidence.

  • Duck dives don't wear you out

    Paddling past a set of waves used to mean getting pushed back to the beach. Now you get through it, stand up on the other side, and still have the legs to catch something on the way back in.

  • You want to turn, not just ride straight

    Standing up in a straight line was the whole goal at first. Wanting to angle down the line, or even attempt a bottom turn, means your board feel has caught up with your balance.

  • Tamarindo's shore break feels small

    This is usually the clearest sign. The wave that used to feel like plenty now feels short, soft, or repetitive — and you find yourself wondering what the coast looks like a little further up or down the beach.

What comes next

None of this means lessons stop being useful — even experienced surfers keep refining technique, and The Foundation still has value once you're catching waves, just with a different focus: turns, timing, reading a face instead of whitewater.

But if two or three of these signs sound familiar, it's usually time to see what's beyond the beach break. The Exploration takes small groups to spots further along the Guanacaste coast — chosen on the day, based on what's actually working, not a fixed itinerary.

Next step

Local Guide

A local's guide to the best surf spots around Tamarindo

Beyond the main beach break — where to go once you're ready to explore the Guanacaste coast.

Local Guide3 min read

Tamarindo's beach break is where most people learn, but it's only one wave among many along this stretch of Guanacaste. Once you can catch and ride green waves on your own, these are the spots worth knowing.

Playa Avellanas

A long, open beach with several peaks spread along it, which means there's usually room to spread out even when it's busy. It handles a range of swell sizes well, which is part of why it's a regular stop on The Exploration.

Playa Grande

Just north of Tamarindo, across the estuary. The wave is a bit more punchy and better shaped on the right tide, with a quieter, more protected feel than the town beach — a good step up once whitewater feels too easy.

Guiones

Further down the coast, near Nosara. Guiones is known for being consistent — it holds a rideable wave more often than most spots nearby, which makes it a reliable option when the closer breaks are flat.

Marbella

Quieter and less built-up than the rest, Marbella works on its own combination of swell and wind. It's not always the first choice, but on the right day it's one of the least crowded waves within reach.

Why the spot changes

Guanacaste has a lot of coastline, and no two beaches work on the same conditions. Rather than committing to a destination in advance, we pick the spot on the day — based on swell, wind and tide — so the group surfs where things are actually lining up, not just where the itinerary says to go.

That's the real difference between a surf tour and a surf transfer: the point was never the drive. It's arriving somewhere that's working.

Trip Planning

How to plan a surf & nature adventure week in Costa Rica

Turning a week in Guanacaste into surf sessions, waterfalls and everything in between.

Trip Planning3 min read

A week in Guanacaste doesn't have to be a week of surfing, or a week of sightseeing — it can be both, in whatever proportion actually suits your group. Here's how to think about planning it.

Start with your surf-to-adventure ratio

Some guests want to surf every morning and treat everything else as a bonus. Others want one or two sessions and the rest of the week exploring waterfalls, volcanic landscapes and the coastline. Neither is more "correct" — the itinerary should follow what you actually want, not the other way around.

Build in rest days on purpose

Paddling every day adds up. A day built around mobility work, a massage or a slower pace isn't wasted time — it's usually what makes the surf sessions on either side of it better.

Pack for both worlds

  • A rash guard for sun and board rash
  • Reef-safe sunscreen
  • Light shoes for uneven trails
  • A dry bag for boat transfers and river crossings
  • A change of clothes that can get muddy
  • A refillable water bottle

Let the day-to-day stay flexible

The same logic that decides which surf spot to visit — swell, wind and tide, checked on the day — applies to the adventure side too. A waterfall hike and a surf session compete for the same window of good weather, so the plan works best when it's allowed to shift a day in either direction.

A sample week

  • Day 1 — Foundation

    Arrive, settle in, and start with a coaching session in Tamarindo to get a read on your level.

  • Day 2 — Exploration

    A guided tour to whichever spot along the coast is working best that day.

  • Day 3 — Adventure

    A waterfall or jungle day, no surfing — just the rest of Guanacaste.

  • Days 4-7 — Mix it up

    Surf, adventure, or a rest day, rebalanced daily depending on conditions and how everyone's feeling.

This is exactly the shape of The Immersion — no fixed itinerary, priced around your group once we know what the week actually looks like.
